title: Apply `D406` and `D407` Ruff rules to be closer to the numpydoc style
body:
In the present ASE, there are many docstrings with
```
Parameters:
```
to indicate the parameters of the functions/methods. However, this is not the correct numpydoc style and not properly rendered. We should fix this as
```
Parameters
----------
```
To do this, in the present MR:

- I set [`D406` (`missing-new-line-after-section-name`)](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/missing-new-line-after-section-name/) and [`D407` (`missing-dashed-underline-after-section`)](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/missing-dashed-underline-after-section/) pydocstyle Ruff rules (e9af39a9d7304594e3b0a8ecc10e7e956cb3e890)
- I run `ruff check --fix` (595ac06092bc69a82248f362104eebae1379665f)
- I fix a few places manually to build docs as expected (f22d9d1d997b5f947e2cbe88fcdd27e63979c283)

This addresses, partly, #68 (partly, because there are many other places with *non*-numpydoc style docstrings).

@askhl, @ajjackson @AndrewRosen Is this the right way to go?

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @askhl and @ajjackson for the review! I have fixed the indentations in `openmx.py` together with minor stylistic docstring updates in 524b93bb71eac13fd4fff10df7299493b9cb43e4.

I also think they did not raise docstring errors likely because they are not called in the present documentation.

I agree we can also re-implement some parts of [OpenMX](https://ase-lib.org/ase/calculators/openmx.html) documentation as docstring, which can be done in a separate MR.

My final hope is to validate docstring in more detail with the `"D"` Ruff option. However, to see the impact of each option, for the moment I would suggest adding them step by step.
